chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding slaves that when one of them commits zina, he is to be lashed fifty lashes, whether he be Muslim, kafir, or Christian; and he is neither to be stoned nor exiled.

key_terms.خَمْسِينَ جَلْدَةً: fifty lashes; the specified hadd in this case
key_terms.زَنَى: committed zina; engaged in unlawful sexual intercourse
key_terms.لَا يُرْجَمُ: he is not stoned; rajm is excluded from this ruling
key_terms.لَا يُنْفَى: he is not exiled; banishment is excluded from this ruling
key_terms.يُجْلَدَ: to be lashed; the corporal punishment prescribed here
key_terms.ٱلْعَبِيدِ: slaves; the legal category discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام on a slave who commits zina?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning the hadd for slaves who commit zina. It states that the punishment is fifty lashes regardless of the slave’s religious affiliation, and that rajm and exile are not applied in this case.
